title: Open a glass studio in Charlottesville: the master path (zoning, building and fire permits, gas service, business license, food and events) and the decisions that shape it
question: I want to open a hot glass studio in Charlottesville with a gas furnace, glory hole, kilns and torches, public classes, and possibly a small cafe or sip-and-blow events. What is the full sequence of city approvals, who do I talk to first, and which decisions change the path?
office: Neighborhood Development Services (Zoning, Development Review, Building Inspections); Fire Marshal's Office; Department of Utilities (Charlottesville Gas) and Utility Billing; Commissioner of the Revenue; Blue Ridge Health District (state); Office of Economic Development
summary: The Charlottesville path, in order: (1) pick a site in a district where an 'Artisan workshop' (the Development Code names glass blowing) is permitted by right: CX, NX, DX, IX and CM, not the residential or RX districts, and not a home occupation; confirm it with NDS Zoning in writing and classify the add-ons (classes, retail, cafe, events). (2) Talk to NDS Development Review early: a change of use into an existing building with no site changes skips Development Review and goes straight to building permits; new construction, additions or site changes need a pre-application conference, a Development Plan and a Final Site Plan; a use marked 'S' needs a Special Use Permit ($2,000 per hearing). (3) Confirm Charlottesville Gas can deliver the furnace load and pressure (Utilities Outreach), apply for the service line and get a commercial quote. (4) Call the Fire Marshal's Office (434-970-3328) with the equipment, oxygen and propane list to learn which operational permits it requires. (5) File the building permit and linked mechanical, gas, electrical and plumbing permits in the City Permit Portal with VCC drawings; pass the inspections, including the gas pressure test and gas unlock; get the certificate of occupancy before using the space. (6) Within 30 days of starting, get the business license from the Commissioner of the Revenue (zoned first; classification set by the office), file the equipment list by March 15, and get a sign permit. (7) If food or drink: Blue Ridge Health District plan review before the cafe is built, the pre-opening inspection after the CO, meals tax registration, and a Virginia ABC licence for alcohol; events bring fire assembly and open-flame permits, temporary use permits for outdoor events, and Parks & Recreation permits for City property. The decision points are: industrial vs. artisan classification (by-right or SUP); cafe or not (health permit, hood, meals tax, FOG); alcohol or not (ABC, accessory-use limits); events or not (assembly permit, occupant load, temporary use permits); new build vs. fit-out (Development Review or not); City gas vs. propane (Utilities vs. LP-gas fire permit).

legal_basis.quote: Enforcement of the provisions of the Building Code for construction and rehabilitation shall be the responsibility of the local building department.
The local governing body of any jurisdiction that enforces the Code may establish such procedures or requirements as may be necessary for the administration and enforcement of the Code.

Each person subject to a license tax shall apply for a license prior to beginning business if he was not subject to licensure in this jurisdiction on or before January 1 of the license year, or no later than March 1 of the license year if he had been issued a license for the preceding year.

No person shall own, establish, conduct, maintain, manage, or operate any hotel, restaurant, summer camp, or campground in this Commonwealth unless the hotel, restaurant, summer camp, or campground is licensed as provided in this chapter.
Prior to occupancy or change of occupancy of a building or structure, a certificate of occupancy shall be obtained in accordance with this section.

Operational permits may be required by the fire official as permitted under the SFPC in accordance with Table 107.2, except that the fire official shall require permits for the manufacturing, storage, handling, use, and sale of explosives.

Typical examples include art studio; ceramic manufacturing; glass blowing; jewelry manufacturing; metalwork; musical instrument manufacturing; leatherwork; and woodworking, cabinet makers or furniture manufacturing.

steps.step: Decision 1: what kind of use is the studio, and where can it go
steps.how: Under the Development Code a glass-blowing studio is an 'Artisan workshop', permitted by right in CX-3, CX-5, CX-8, NX-3, NX-5, NX-8, NX-10, DX, IX-5, IX-8 and CM, and not allowed in R-A, RN-A, R-B, R-C, RX-3, RX-5 or CV. A home occupation cannot host a furnace (no equipment beyond what a home has, no hazardous materials, no noise or odor beyond the dwelling, no on-site retail). If NDS instead reads a gas-fired hot shop with oxygen and propane as 'industrial and manufacturing', the by-right districts narrow (low-impact up to 4,000 SF in CX-3, CX-5, NX-3, NX-5, NX-8, IX-5, IX-8 and CM) or a Special Use Permit is needed (high-impact in IX-5 and IX-8 only). Classes, retail, a cafe and events are classified separately. Get the classification in writing before leasing. Full detail: glass_studio_zoning_use.
steps.deadline: A zoning determination must be answered within 90 days (Va. Code § 15.2-2286(A)(4))
steps.fee: Zoning Compliance Letter (mixed use/commercial) $250 as printed in the NDS Fee Schedule
steps.quote: A use that provides a work space for artists or artisans that may include the production of hand-crafted products.

steps.step: Decision 2: fit out an existing building, or build or change the site
steps.how: A change of use into an existing building with no change to site access skips Development Review and goes straight to the building permit, where zoning is checked. New construction, additions, site changes (new paving, loading, outdoor propane tank pads) or changed access need Development Review: a required pre-application conference with the Administrator and the Development Review Team, then a Development Plan ($400) and a Final Site Plan (Minor $800, Major $1,800 plus per-unit and per-100-SF charges) before any building permit. A Special Use Permit, if needed, also starts with a pre-application conference and costs $2,000 per public hearing. In a historic or Entrance Corridor overlay, exterior changes and signs need a Certificate of Appropriateness. The pre-application conference is the one meeting to ask for first; the NDS front desk (434-970-3182) and Development Review mailbox can set it up.
steps.deadline: Development Plans: 21-day review cycles; Minor Final Site Plans: three 21-day reviews and a 14-day final
steps.fee: Development Plan Review $400; Final Site Plan Review Minor $800 / Major $1,800; Special Use Permit $2,000 per public hearing
steps.quote: Projects that do not meet thresholds in Section 345.2.9—such as one or twounit homes or small alterations without public improvements—may go directly to Building Permit review. A change of use does not require Development Review if it does not alter site access or require new access improvements.

steps.step: Decision 3: City natural gas or propane for the furnace and glory hole
steps.who: Operator; Utilities Outreach (434-970-3812); Fire Marshal's Office
steps.how: Charlottesville Gas serves most city streets. Contact Utilities Outreach to confirm availability for the connected load and to request elevated pressure in writing (the standard is 7 inches of water column; PSIG service is for commercial and industrial customers and needs the Gas Engineer's approval). Apply for the service line with the electronic form and expect a customized commercial quote; the published $340 fee (rising to $1,950 on January 1, 2027) is for homes with a furnace or water heater. If the load or pressure cannot be met, propane needs tanks and piping under the City gas permit and a Fire Marshal LP-gas operational permit, and the Development Code's industrial definitions count 'significant use of highly combustible or flammable' gases against a low-impact classification. Water and sewer connections, slurry handling, stormwater and DEQ air pointers are in glass_studio_utilities_and_environment.
steps.deadline: About 4 weeks for the service line after payment, then about 10 days to the meter (service guide, residential)
steps.fee: Commercial gas service line: customized quote; meter set fee $30; commercial deposit by quote
steps.quote: Gas service is available to most streets within Charlottesville City limits, and limited service is available to urban areas of Albemarle County.

steps.step: Call the Fire Marshal's Office before the plans are final
steps.how: The City publishes no fire operational-permit list or forms. Under the Statewide Fire Prevention Code the fire official may require permits for hot work (fixed hot work equipment, portable hot work equipment inside a structure, and public demonstrations), compressed gases above 504 cubic feet of oxygen or 200 cubic feet of flammable gas, LP-gas, industrial ovens, open flames in assembly or dining areas, places of assembly and commercial cooking. Ask which apply, the fee and whether a Hot Work Program permit is available, and plan cylinder and tank storage with them. Fire protection systems must then be inspected and reported through IROL. Full detail: glass_studio_fire_permits.
steps.deadline: SFPC permits are issued after inspection and before the activity starts
steps.fee: Not published; set by City ordinance

steps.step: Building, mechanical, gas, electrical and plumbing permits, inspections and the certificate of occupancy
steps.who: Operator with licensed contractors and a design professional; NDS Building Inspections
steps.how: Apply in the City Public Permit Portal for the building permit (VCC drawings showing the furnace, glory hole, kilns, exhaust, fuel-gas and oxygen piping, electrical loads and egress), then linked Mechanical, Gas, Electrical and Plumbing permits, and a Commercial Kitchen Hood (Type 1) permit if the cafe has grease-producing cooking. Fees are $75 minimum per permit plus value-based charges, a $10 to $50 maintenance fee and the 2% state levy. Request inspections in the portal; gas lines are inspected under pressure before connection, and the gas meter is unlocked the next business day after the final passes. The certificate of occupancy follows the approved final within five working days and nothing may be used before it. Full detail: glass_studio_building_mechanical.
steps.deadline: Certificate of occupancy within five working days of the approved final inspection
steps.fee: $75 minimum per permit; $75 plus project value x BR above $1,500; maintenance fee $10 to $50; 2% state levy; Not Ready and reinspection fees $100
steps.quote: The City Public Permit Portal is available for submitting building and trade permits, as well as all payment of all permit fees and requesting inspections. Guest access is also available for tracking permits and inspections.

steps.step: Business license, equipment returns and the sign
steps.who: Operator; Commissioner of the Revenue (434-970-3170); NDS Zoning (sign permit)
steps.how: Apply within the first thirty days of establishing the business (state law: before beginning), with the New Business License Checklist items (EIN, Virginia sales tax number, SCC registration, occupancy permit, health permit if food). The first year's tax is on estimated gross receipts per activity: $35 under $50,000, $50 to $100,000, then a classification rate the Commissioner sets; a manufacturer selling at wholesale at the place of manufacture is exempt under state law, but retail sales are not. File the business tangible property list (or the machinery and tools return if treated as a manufacturer) by March 15 each year, taxed at 4.4% of assessed value. A permanent sign needs a $100 sign permit. Full detail: glass_studio_business_license.
steps.deadline: Business license within thirty days of establishing the business; renewal by March 1; property return by March 15
steps.fee: $35 or $50 below $100,000 of gross receipts per activity; sign permit $100 per sign
steps.quote: Applications are due within the first thirty days of establishing business.

steps.who: Operator; Blue Ridge Health District (434-972-6219); Commissioner of the Revenue; Virginia ABC; Fire Marshal's Office; NDS Zoning; Parks & Recreation
steps.how: A cafe needs Blue Ridge Health District plan review before it is built (apply at least 30 days before opening or renovation), a pre-opening inspection that requires the City occupancy permit, and the annual VDH permit; the City's 7% meals tax is registered with the business license and filed monthly. Alcohol needs a Virginia ABC licence, and the Development Code lets a food and beverage or indoor entertainment use serve it only as an accessory use. Events bring the fire official's place-of-assembly and open-flame permits and the building's occupant load; outdoor events on the lot need a $250 Temporary Use Permit (at most 5 a year); events on City streets or parks go through Parks & Recreation ($25, 30 or 60 days ahead). Food at a one-off event needs a $40 Temporary Food Establishment permit unless the studio already holds a permanent permit. Full detail: glass_studio_food_and_events.
steps.deadline: Health plan review before construction; VDH permit application at least 30 days before opening; TFE applications 10 days before an event
steps.fee: VDH plan review $40 and annual permit $40 (district page: $80 application); TFE $40; meals tax 7%; Temporary Use Permit $250; special event application $25
steps.quote: Per the Virginia Food Regulations , owner of record must apply at least 30 days prior to opening to the public or start of renovation.

steps.step: Use the City's business help and keep every approval current
steps.who: Operator; Office of Economic Development; each office above
steps.how: The Office of Economic Development (434-970-3110, ecodev@charlottesville.gov) runs GO Start-Up training and GO Hire grants. Once open: renew the business license by March 1 and file the property return by March 15; file meals tax by the 20th monthly; keep fire operational permits on the premises and have fire systems inspected on schedule; keep the certificate of occupancy's use and occupant load; and treat any expansion (more seats, a bigger furnace, a new building) as a new change of use or permit. Report business changes or closure to the Commissioner at charlottesville.gov/cor/bizchange.
steps.quote: The Office of Economic Development is the catalyst for public and private initiatives that create employment opportunities and a vibrant and sustainable economy.

escalation.quote: Pursuant to the provisions of Virginia Code Section 58.1-3703.1(A)(5), any taxpayer assessed with a local business license tax as the result of an appealable event may apply within one year from the last day of the tax year for which such assessment is made, or within one year from the date of such appealable event to the Commissioner of the Revenue.

caveats: This overview orders the sub-processes; each has its own file with the full legal basis, forms, fees, contacts and escalation: glass_studio_zoning_use, glass_studio_building_mechanical, glass_studio_fire_permits, glass_studio_business_license, glass_studio_food_and_events and glass_studio_utilities_and_environment.

The City of Charlottesville publishes no checklist, guide or page for opening a studio, makerspace or manufacturing business; the sequence here is assembled from the Development Code, the NDS, Fire, Utilities and Commissioner pages, and state law. The 'who to talk to first' answer (NDS Zoning for the use, then a Development Review pre-application conference) is an inference from those pages, not a City statement.

Three things no City page settles and only the offices can: how NDS classifies a gas-fired hot shop (artisan workshop vs. industrial), which fire operational permits the Fire Marshal's Office requires and at what fee, and what Charlottesville Gas will charge to serve the furnace load at elevated pressure.
All fees are as published on 2026-10-19; the NDS Fee Schedule is a scanned PDF and several rows are hard to read.
Sites in the Albemarle County part of greater Charlottesville follow Albemarle County's processes instead (the Albemarle website's terms forbid reprinting; not researched here).
State processes (Virginia sales tax, SCC registration, ABC licensing, DEQ air permits, DPOR) are pointed to but not modeled.
